summary: Karanjwa, the falls the Mahal-campsite crowd calls 'Mahal waterfall', a monsoon drop in the Subir belt between the Girmal country and Bhalkhet.
description:
Karanjwa carries two names: the map's, and 'Mahal waterfall', the label the eco-campsite crowd attached because Mahal is where most visitors are staying when they hear about it. The falls actually sit a proper drive south-west of the campsite, in the same Subir-belt forest country as Bhalkhet, Milan and Dev Van, and together the four make the belt the densest little waterfall cluster in the district.

It keeps the belt's terms: monsoon-fed flow, a short walk from village roads, forest framing, and no facilities of any kind. Campsite guides at Mahal know the way and will pair it with Girmal or the U-turn point for guests wanting a fuller falls day.
highlights: The 'Mahal waterfall' of campsite word-of-mouth, under its own name
Part of the Subir belt's four-fall cluster
Pairs with Girmal and the U-turn point from Mahal

modes.road: Village roads in the Subir belt between the Mahal–Girmal side and Godadiya; ask at Subir or the Mahal campsite
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short forest walk from the road end; slippery in the rains

visit.notes: Open forest site; go with a campsite guide if you are staying at Mahal.

seasonality.notes: Runs with the rains; a trickle by winter's end.

experience.photography_notes: Forest gloom rewards steady hands; the fall reads best with bamboo kept in frame.

amenities.food: None, the Mahal campsite kitchen (order ahead) or Subir are nearest
amenities.guides: Mahal campsite guides know the falls; recommended

warnings: Do not cross swollen streams on the approach in spate
Leech protection and grip footwear through the monsoon window

tips: From a Mahal stay, do Girmal and the U-turn point one day and the Karanjwa–Milan–Bhalkhet belt the next
Ask for 'Karanjwa dhodh': the 'Mahal waterfall' name only works at the campsite

faqs.q: Is Karanjwa the same as 'Mahal waterfall'?
faqs.a: Yes. One falls, two names. 'Mahal waterfall' is campsite shorthand; Karanjwa is what the map and villages call it, a drive south-west of the campsite itself.

nearby.note: The stay that gave the falls its nickname
